text: At 298 K , the mole percentage of $\mathrm{N}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ in air is $80%$. Water is in equilibrium with air at a pressure of 10 atm . What is the mole fraction of $\mathrm{N}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ in water at 298 K ? $(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{H}}$ for $\mathrm{N}_{2}$ is $\left. 6.5\times 10^{7}\mathrm{mm}\mathrm{Hg}\right )$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The partial pressure of a gas in air is its mole fraction times the total pressure (Dalton's law):

$p_{\mathrm{N}{}_{2}}=0.80\times 10\text{atm}=8\text{atm}$

Since $K_{H}$ is given in mm Hg, the pressure is converted with $1\text{atm}=760\text{mm Hg}$:

$p_{\mathrm{N}{}_{2}}=8\times 760=6080\text{mm Hg}$

Henry's law, $p=K_{H}x$, gives the mole fraction of $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}$ dissolved in water:

$x_{\mathrm{N}{}_{2}}=\dfrac{p_{\mathrm{N}{}_{2}}}{K_{H}}=\dfrac{6080}{6.5\times 10^{7}}=9.35\times 10^{-5}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: The heat of atomisation of methane and ethane are ' x ' $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and ' y ' $\mathrm{kJ}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The longest wavelength ( $λ$ ) of light capable of breaking the $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$ bond can be expressed in SI unit as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For methane:

$\Delta H_{\text{atom}}(CH_{4})=x=4D(\text{C–H})\Rightarrow D(\text{C–H})=\frac{x}{4}$

For ethane:

$\Delta H_{\text{atom}}(C_{2}H_{6})=y=6D(\text{C–H})+D(\text{C–C})$

$\Rightarrow \quad D(\text{C–C})=y-6\left (\frac{x}{4}\right )=y-\frac{6x}{4}=\frac{4y-6x}{4}(\text{kJ mol}^{-1})$

Energy per molecule needed to break the C–C bond:

$E=\frac{D(\text{C–C})\times 1000}{N_{A}}(\text{J})$

Longest wavelength corresponds to minimum photon energy:

$\frac{hc}{λ}=E\Rightarrow λ=\frac{N_{A}hc}{1000D(\text{C–C})}$

$λ=\frac{N_{A}hc}{1000\left (\frac{4y-6x}{4}\right )}=\frac{N_{A}hc}{250(4y-6x)}$

Correct option: D.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Pair of species among the following having same bond order as well as paramagnetic character will be-
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Bond order $=\dfrac{1}{2}(N_{b}-N_{a})$, counting the $1s$ electrons; a species with an unpaired electron is paramagnetic. Up to 14 electrons $π_{2p}$ lies below $σ_{2p_{z}}$, beyond 14 electrons $σ_{2p_{z}}$ lies below $π_{2p}$.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (13 electrons): $σ_{2p_{z}}$ holds one electron, $N_{b}=9$, $N_{a}=4$, bond order 2.5, paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ (15 electrons): one electron in $π^{\ast }$, $N_{b}=10$, $N_{a}=5$, bond order 2.5, paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{2-}$ (16 electrons): $(π_{2p_{x}}^{\ast })^{1}(π_{2p_{y}}^{\ast })^{1}$, $N_{b}=10$, $N_{a}=6$, bond order 2, paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ (15 electrons): $N_{b}=10$, $N_{a}=5$, bond order 2.5, paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ (17 electrons): $N_{b}=10$, $N_{a}=7$, bond order 1.5, paramagnetic.

The pairs have bond orders (A) 1.5 and 2.5, (B) 2.5 and 2, (C) 1.5 and 2.5, (D) 2.5 and 2.5; only $\mathrm{O}{}_{2}{}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{N}{}_{2}{}^{-}$ match in bond order while both are paramagnetic.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
Consider the following gaseous equilibrium in a closed container of volume ' $V$ ' at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$.

$\mathrm{P}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{Q}_{2}(\mathrm{g})⇌2\mathrm{PQ}(\mathrm{g})$

2 moles each of $\mathrm{P}_{2}(\mathrm{g}),\mathrm{Q}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ and $\mathrm{PQ}(\mathrm{g})$ are present at equilibrium. Now one mole each of ' $\mathrm{P}_{2}$ ' and ' $\mathrm{Q}_{2}$ ' are added to the equilibrium keeping the temperature at $\mathrm{T}(\mathrm{K})$. The number of moles of $\mathrm{P}_{2},\mathrm{Q}_{2}$ and PQ at the new equilibrium, respectively, are
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $\mathrm{P}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{Q}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})2\mathrm{PQ}(\mathrm{g})$, $\Delta n_{g}=0$, so the volume cancels:

$K_{c}=\dfrac{n_{\mathrm{PQ}}^{2}}{n_{\mathrm{P}_{2}}n_{\mathrm{Q}_{2}}}$

At the first equilibrium, $K_{c}=\dfrac{2^{2}}{2\times 2}=1$.

Just after adding 1 mol each of $\mathrm{P}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{Q}{}_{2}$: $n_{\mathrm{P}_{2}}=n_{\mathrm{Q}_{2}}=3$ mol and $n_{\mathrm{PQ}}=2$ mol, so $Q_{c}=\dfrac{2^{2}}{3\times 3}=\dfrac{4}{9}<K_{c}$ and the reaction moves forward by $x$ mol:

$\dfrac{(2+2x)^{2}}{(3-x)^{2}}=1\Rightarrow 2+2x=3-x\Rightarrow x=\dfrac{1}{3}$

At the new equilibrium, $n_{\mathrm{P}_{2}}=n_{\mathrm{Q}_{2}}=3-\dfrac{1}{3}=\dfrac{8}{3}\approx 2.67$ mol and $n_{\mathrm{PQ}}=2+\dfrac{2}{3}=\dfrac{8}{3}\approx 2.67$ mol.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: The correct order of $\mathrm{C},\mathrm{N},\mathrm{O}$ and F in terms of second ionisation potential is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The second ionisation removes an electron from the unipositive ion: $\mathrm{C}{}^{+}$ $[\text{He}]2s^{2}2p^{1}$, $\mathrm{N}{}^{+}$ $[\text{He}]2s^{2}2p^{2}$, $\mathrm{O}{}^{+}$ $[\text{He}]2s^{2}2p^{3}$, $\mathrm{F}{}^{+}$ $[\text{He}]2s^{2}2p^{4}$.

Across the period the nuclear charge increases, so $\mathrm{IE}_{2}$ increases from C to N to F; fluorine, with the highest nuclear charge, has a larger $\mathrm{IE}_{2}$ than nitrogen even though $\mathrm{F}{}^{2+}$ formed is half-filled.

$\mathrm{O}{}^{+}$ has the extra-stable half-filled $2p^{3}$ configuration, while the electron removed from $\mathrm{F}{}^{+}$ ($2p^{4}$) is a paired electron that suffers extra repulsion, so $\mathrm{IE}_{2}(\mathrm{O})$ is slightly greater than $\mathrm{IE}_{2}(\mathrm{F})$.

Values ($\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$): C 2353, N 2856, F 3374, O 3388, giving

$\mathrm{C}<\mathrm{N}<\mathrm{F}<\mathrm{O}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Cross aldol condensation between two different aldehydes will always produce four different products.

Statement II : When semicarbazide reacts with a mixture of benzaldehyde and acetophenone under optimum pH , it forms a condensation product with acetophenone only.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I: False.  

A crossed aldol between two different aldehydes gives four products only in the uncontrolled case when both aldehydes have α‑H (2 self‑aldols + 2 crossed). It is not “always”: e.g., benzaldehyde (no α‑H) cannot self‑aldol, so fewer products result; and under controlled conditions you can also avoid mixtures.

Statement II: False.  

Semicarbazide forms semicarbazones with both aldehydes and ketones, and aldehydes (benzaldehyde) generally react faster than ketones (acetophenone) under the usual “optimum pH” conditions. So it will not give a condensation product with acetophenone only.

Correct option: B — Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: The wavelength of spectral line obtained in the spectrum of $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$ ion, when the transition takes place between two levels whose sum is 4 and difference is 2 , is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From $n_{1}+n_{2}=4$ and $n_{2}-n_{1}=2$: $n_{2}=3$ and $n_{1}=1$. For $\mathrm{Li}{}^{2+}$, $Z=3$.

$\dfrac{1}{λ}=R_{H}Z^{2}\left (\dfrac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\dfrac{1}{n_{2}^{2}}\right )=R_{H}\times 9\times \left (1-\dfrac{1}{9}\right )=8R_{H}$

With $R_{H}=1.097\times 10^{7}\text{m}^{-1}=1.097\times 10^{5}\text{cm}^{-1}$:

$λ=\dfrac{1}{8\times 1.097\times 10^{5}}\text{cm}=1.14\times 10^{-6}\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution at temperature T K . At T K , the vapour pressures of pure A and B are 55 and $15\mathrm{kN}\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ respectively. What is the mole fraction of A in solution of A and B in equilibrium with a vapour in which the mole fraction of A is 0.8?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an ideal solution, Raoult’s law applies:

$p_{A}=x_{A}P_{A}^{\ast },p_{B}=x_{B}P_{B}^{\ast }$

Total pressure:

$P=p_{A}+p_{B}=55x_{A}+15(1-x_{A})=55x_{A}+15-15x_{A}=40x_{A}+15$

Vapour-phase mole fraction (Dalton’s law):

$y_{A}=\frac{p_{A}}{P}=\frac{55x_{A}}{40x_{A}+15}=0.8$

Solve:

$55x_{A}=0.8(40x_{A}+15)=32x_{A}+12$

$23x_{A}=12\Rightarrow x_{A}=\frac{12}{23}=0.5217$

Answer: 0.5217 (Option A)
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
From the following, how many compounds contain at least one secondary alcohol?


[IMG]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A secondary alcohol carries the $-\mathrm{OH}$ group on a carbon atom bonded to exactly two other carbon atoms.

(I) $\mathrm{HOOC}-\mathrm{N}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}){}_{2}$: both alcoholic $-\mathrm{OH}$ groups are on $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}$ carbons (primary); the remaining $-\mathrm{OH}$ belongs to the carboxyl group.

(II) Butane-1,2-diol, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$: C-2 is bonded to the ethyl carbon and the $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$ carbon, so it is a secondary alcohol.

(III) The ring carbon bearing $-\mathrm{OH}$ is bonded to two ring carbons and the side-chain carbon, and the side-chain carbon to the ring carbon and two methyl groups; both alcohols are tertiary.

(IV) The side-chain $\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})$ (bonded to a ring carbon and $\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$) and the ring $\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})$ (bonded to two ring carbons) are secondary; the ring carbon carrying $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{OH}$ is tertiary.

(V) 3-Methylpentane-2,3-diol, $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{OH})(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}$: C-2 is secondary (C-3 is tertiary).

(VI) 2,3-Dimethylbutane-1,2,3-triol, $\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3})(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}){}_{2}\mathrm{OH}$: C-2 and C-3 are each bonded to three carbon atoms (tertiary) and C-1 is primary, so there is no secondary alcohol.

Compounds II, IV and V contain at least one secondary alcohol, which makes three.

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: The number of possible tripeptides formed involving alanine (ala), glycine (gly) and valine (val), where no amino acid has been used more than once is:
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
A tripeptide in which ala, gly and val are each used at most once must contain all three, one of each, so the count equals the number of orders of three different residues: $3!=6$.

A peptide chain has a direction: it is written from the residue with the free amino group (N-terminus) to the residue with the free carboxyl group (C-terminus). So Gly-Ala-Val (free amino group on gly) and Val-Ala-Gly (free amino group on val) are different compounds, not one chain read backwards.

The six tripeptides are Gly-Ala-Val, Gly-Val-Ala, Ala-Gly-Val, Ala-Val-Gly, Val-Gly-Ala and Val-Ala-Gly.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: One mole of $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$ was passed into 2 L of cold 2 M KOH solution. After the reaction, the concentrations of $\mathrm{Cl}^{-},\mathrm{ClO}^{-}$and $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$are respectively (assume volume remains constant)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In cold KOH, chlorine disproportionates:

$\mathrm{Cl}_{2}+2\mathrm{OH}^{-}\to \mathrm{Cl}^{-}+\mathrm{ClO}^{-}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Initial moles of $\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ in $2\text{L}$ of $2\text{M}$ KOH:

$n(\mathrm{OH}^{-})=2\times 2=4\text{mol}$

Given $1$ mol $\mathrm{Cl}_{2}$:

$\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ consumed $=2\times 1=2$ mol  

$\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ formed $=1$ mol  

$\mathrm{ClO}^{-}$ formed $=1$ mol  

$\mathrm{OH}^{-}$ remaining $=4-2=2$ mol

Assuming volume stays $2\text{L}$:

$[\mathrm{Cl}^{-}]=\frac{1}{2}=0.5\text{M},[\mathrm{ClO}^{-}]=\frac{1}{2}=0.5\text{M},[\mathrm{OH}^{-}]=\frac{2}{2}=1\text{M}$

Answer: Option C — $0.5\text{M},0.5\text{M},1\text{M}$.

text:
Find out the statements which are not true.

A. Resonating structures with more number of covalent bonds and lesser charge separation are more stable.

B. In electromeric effect, an unsaturated system shows +E effect with nucleophile and -E effect with electrophile.

C. Inductive effect is responsible for high melting point, boiling point and dipole moment of polar compounds.

D. The greater the number of alkyl groups attached to the doubly bonded carbon atoms, higher is the heat of hydrogenation.

E. Stability of carbanion increases with the increase in $\mathrm{s}-$ character of the carbon carrying the negative charge.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A is true: resonating structures with more covalent bonds and less separation of opposite charges are more stable.

Statement B is false: in the $+E$ effect the $π$ electrons move to the atom to which the attacking reagent gets attached, which happens with electrophiles (e.g. $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ adding to an alkene); in the $-E$ effect they move to the atom to which the reagent does not get attached, which happens with nucleophiles (e.g. $\mathrm{CN}{}^{-}$ adding to a carbonyl group). The statement reverses the two.

Statement C is true: the permanent bond polarisation caused by the inductive effect gives polar compounds their dipole moment and the stronger intermolecular attractions behind their higher melting and boiling points.

Statement D is false: alkyl groups on the doubly bonded carbons stabilise the alkene by hyperconjugation, so more alkyl groups mean a lower heat of hydrogenation.

Statement E is true: greater s-character holds the lone pair closer to the nucleus, so carbanion stability increases in the order $sp^{3}<sp^{2}<sp$.

The statements that are not true are B and D.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text: Grignard reagent $\mathrm{RMgBr}(\mathrm{P})$ reacts with water and forms a gas $(\mathrm{Q})$. One gram of Q occupies $1.4\mathrm{dm}^{3}$ at STP. (P) on reaction with dry ice in dry ether followed by $\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}$forms a compound (Z). 0.1 mole of (Z) will weigh $____$ g. (Nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With water, a Grignard reagent gives the corresponding hydrocarbon:

$\mathrm{RMgBr}+\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}\to \mathrm{RH}(\mathrm{Q})+\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{OH})\mathrm{Br}$

Given 1 g of $Q$ occupies $1.4\text{dm}^{3}$ at STP.

Moles in $1.4\text{dm}^{3}$:

$n=\frac{1.4}{22.4}=0.0625\text{mol}$

So molar mass of $Q$:

$M=\frac{1}{0.0625}=16\text{g mol}^{-1}$

A hydrocarbon gas with molar mass 16 is methane, $\mathrm{CH}_{4}$. Hence $R=\mathrm{CH}_{3}$, and $P=\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}$.

Carboxylation with dry ice followed by acid workup gives:

$\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{MgBr}\leftarrow _{\mathrm{ether}}^{\mathrm{CO}_{2}}\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COO}^{-}\mathrm{MgBr}\leftarrow ^{\mathrm{H}_{3}\mathrm{O}^{+}}\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}(\mathrm{Z})$

So $Z$ is acetic acid, $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$, with molar mass $60\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

Mass of $0.1$ mol:

$0.1\times 60=6\text{g}$

Answer: 6 g

text:
Molar conductivity of a weak acid HQ of concentration 0.18 M was found to be $1/30$ of the molar conductivity of another weak acid HZ with concentration of 0.02 M . If $λ^{\circ }\mathrm{Q}^{-}$ happened to be equal with $λ^{\circ }\mathrm{Z}^{-}$, then the difference of the $\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}$ values of the two weak acids $(\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HQ})-\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HZ}))$ is $____$ (Nearest integer).

[Given: degree of dissociation $(α)\ll 1$ for both weak acids, $λ^{\circ }$ : limiting molar conductivity of ions]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{ll} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HQ})=\mathrm{C}_{1}α_{1}^{2} & α_{1}=\frac{λ_{\mathrm{m}}(\mathrm{HQ})}{λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty }(\mathrm{HQ})} \\ \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HZ})=\mathrm{C}_{2}α_{2}^{2} & α_{2}=\frac{λ_{\mathrm{m}}(\mathrm{HZ})}{λ_{\mathrm{m}}^{\infty }(\mathrm{HZ})} \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HQ})}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HZ})}=\dfrac{\mathrm{C}_{1}}{\mathrm{C}_{2}}\cdot \left (\dfrac{α_{1}}{α_{2}}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{0.18}{0.02}\cdot \left [\dfrac{λ_{\mathrm{m}}(\mathrm{HQ})}{λ_{\mathrm{m}}(\mathrm{HZ})}\right ]^{2} \\ \dfrac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HQ})}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HZ})}=9\times \left (\dfrac{1}{30}\right )^{2}=\dfrac{1}{100} \\ \mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HQ})-\mathrm{pK}_{\mathrm{a}}(\mathrm{HZ})=2 \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
A chromium complex with a formula $\mathrm{CrCl}_{3}\cdot 6\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ has a spin only magnetic moment value of 3.87 BM and its solution conductivity corresponds to $1:2$ electrolyte. 2.75 g of the complex solution was initially passed through a cation exchanger. The solution obtained after the process was reacted with excess of $\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}$. The amount of AgCl formed in the above process is $____$ g. (Nearest integer)

[Given: Molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{Cr}:52;\mathrm{Cl}:35.5,\mathrm{Ag}:108,\mathrm{O}:16,\mathrm{H}:1$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Spin-only moment $μ=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=3.87\text{BM}$ gives $n=3$, consistent with $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ ($3d^{3}$).

A 1:2 electrolyte has a dipositive complex cation and two ionisable $\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, so the complex is $[\mathrm{CrCl}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{5}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}\cdot \mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

Molar mass $=52+3(35.5)+6(18)=266.5\text{g mol}^{-1}$, so moles of complex $=\dfrac{2.75}{266.5}=0.01032\text{mol}$.

The cation exchanger retains $[\mathrm{CrCl}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{5}]{}^{2+}$ (with its coordinated chloride) and releases $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$, so the solution carries only the two ionisable chloride ions per formula unit.

$n(\mathrm{AgCl})=2\times 0.01032=0.02064\text{mol}$

$m(\mathrm{AgCl})=0.02064\times 143.5=2.96\text{g}\approx 3\text{g}$

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
The half-life of ${}^{65}\mathrm{Zn}$ is 245 days. After $x$ days, $75%$ of original activity remained. The value of $x$ in days is $____$ . (Nearest integer)

(Given: $\log 3=0.4771$ and $\log 2=0.3010$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}_{1/2}=\dfrac{\ln 2}{\mathrm{K}} \end{array}$

Here, $\mathrm{t}_{1/2}=245$ days, so we find $K$ as:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{K}=\dfrac{\ln 2}{245} \end{array}$

Now we use the radioactive decay relation for activity:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}=\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{K}}\ln \dfrac{\mathrm{a}_{0}}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{t}}} \end{array}$

Given that $75%$ of the original activity remains, so $\mathrm{a}_{t}=0.75\mathrm{a}_{0}=\frac{3}{4}\mathrm{a}_{0}$.

So,

$\begin{array}{l} \dfrac{\mathrm{a}_{0}}{\mathrm{a}_{\mathrm{t}}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{a}_{0}}{\frac{3}{4}\mathrm{a}_{0}}=\dfrac{4}{3} \end{array}$

Therefore,

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}_{25%}=\dfrac{1}{\mathrm{K}}\ln \dfrac{4}{3} \end{array}$

Substitute $\mathrm{K}=\frac{\ln 2}{245}$:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}_{25%}=\dfrac{1}{\frac{\ln 2}{245}}\ln \dfrac{4}{3} \end{array}$

Simplifying:

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{t}_{25%}=245\dfrac{\ln \frac{4}{3}}{\ell \mathrm{n}2}=245\left [\dfrac{2\log 2-\log 3}{\log 2}\right ] \end{array}$

Now use the given values $\log 3=0.4771$ and $\log 2=0.3010$:

$\begin{array}{l} =245\left [\dfrac{2\times 0.3010-0.4771}{0.3010}\right ]=101.66\text{day.} \end{array}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift

text:
0.25 g of an organic compound "A" containing carbon, hydrogen and oxygen was analysed using the combustion method. There was an increase in mass of $\mathrm{CaCl}_{2}$ tube and potash tube at the end of the experiment. The amount was found to be 0.15 g and 0.1837 g , respectively. The percentage of oxygen in compound A is

$____$ %. (Nearest integer)

(Given: molar mass in $\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}\mathrm{H}:1,\mathrm{C}:12,\mathrm{O}:16$ )
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From combustion:

Increase in mass of CaCl₂ tube = mass of H₂O formed  

$m(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})=0.15\text{g},n(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})=\frac{0.15}{18}=0.008333\text{mol}$

Moles of H atoms:

$n(\text{H})=2n(\text{H}_{2}\text{O})=0.016667\text{mol}$

Mass of H:

$m(\text{H})=0.016667\times 1=0.016667\text{g}$

Increase in mass of potash tube = mass of CO₂ formed  

$m(\text{CO}_{2})=0.1837\text{g},n(\text{CO}_{2})=\frac{0.1837}{44}=0.004175\text{mol}$

Moles of C atoms = moles of CO₂:

$n(\text{C})=0.004175\text{mol}$

Mass of C:

$m(\text{C})=0.004175\times 12=0.05010\text{g}$

Sample mass = 0.25 g, so mass of oxygen in the compound:

$m(\text{O})=0.25-(0.016667+0.05010)=0.18323\text{g}$

Percentage of oxygen:

$%\text{O}=\frac{0.18323}{0.25}\times 100=73.29%\approx 73%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2026 (Online) 24th January Evening Shift
